body:
We run long-running agent workflows and use WorkflowPanicPolicy: FailWorkflow because we prefer immediate failure over indefinite retry loops from BlockWorkflow.

We rely on defers inside our workflow function for critical cleanup.

We noticed that:

- When a Go panic occurs inside the workflow function (e.g., nil pointer), the defers do run before the workflow is marked as failed. Users see "stopped" immediately.

- When a non-deterministic error is detected (e.g., after a code change during replay), the defers do not run. The workflow is marked as failed but the "stopped" heartbeat is never sent. Users see the job as "running" until a separate TTL timeout catches it.

Is there a recommended way to run cleanup logic (like sending a final heartbeat or notifying an external service) when FailWorkflow triggers on a non-deterministic error?

comments.body:
If non-determinisim is detected that means the workflow can't restore its state so it cannot generate any new commands, or very likely even run your workflow code to the point where you called these `defers`. If you want to run some logic after a workflow fails the best way currently is to run your workflow as a child workflow and have the parent run any compensation.

If you have any other questions I'd recommend using our Slack or Community forum for questions https://temporal.io/community

title: How to run cleanup when FailWorkflow panic policy triggers on non-deterministic error?
